content.title: Volkswagen's third-quarter sales lifted by Europe and EVs
content.summary:
STORY: Volkswagen Group's release of new models paid off in the third quarter.

The German auto giant reported a 1% rise in deliveries during the period on Friday.

It said a boost from Europe and South America pushed back on pressure from China and the U.S..

Group deliveries to China fell 7%.

VW isn't the only German major to see a sales decline in the country recently.

Mercedes' was down by more than a quarter over the same period, while BMW also saw a slight drop.

Electric vehicles were a bright spot for VW in the third quarter.

Deliveries of battery EVs rose by a third from July to September.

It saw a big 213% jump in North America and a 60% rise in Europe of battery EVs.

But sales of battery EVs plunged by more than half in China.

One analyst said this was due to the varying market conditions in the three markets.

The results come a day after Volkswagen's Porsche unit said sales were down in China by more than a quarter in the first nine months of the year.

VW slashed its financial guidance for this year in September.

content.title: Ferrari’s EV Reveal: A Top for the Stock? Sizing Up Thursday’s Plunge.
content.summary: MARANELLO, Italy—  Ferrari  gave investors a glimpse of its first electric model on Wednesday, at a presentation here that felt more like something out of the Tron sci-fi franchise than a luxury launch event.  Laser beams and pounding industrial music accompanied Ferrari’s reveal of the Elettrica’s chassis, motor, and battery pack, as well as a built-in system that amplifies the sounds of the electric engine in a bid to replicate the feeling that drivers get when they hear the visceral roar of a traditional supercar.  The problem was that Ferrari also unveiled its financial projections for the rest of this decade, and they were lower than expected.

content.title: Porsche’s Sliding Sales Deepen German Automotive Malaise
content.summary: Porsche on Thursday joined BMW and Mercedes-Benz in reporting weaker sales in China, where local competitors led by BYD Co. and Xiaomi Corp. are winning over buyers with competitively priced electric vehicles.  BMW earlier this week cut its earnings outlook after demand in the world’s biggest auto market fell short of expectations.  The China struggles add to US tariff costs and stagnant sales in Europe, squeezing Germany’s carmakers across their three core markets.
